summary: Proceed only with source B and the B2-B4 cells rebuilt on a rules-clean mechanism. The per-call save/set/restore of torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library breaks standing policy and must go; in its place, port the prepare-time cuBLASLt extension (_LT_CPP, impl a77cdec6, which already ran clean in scored job 26a8be34), query its heuristic at the workspace caps and descriptor settings torch's Lt path uses, and hold the chosen algo row plus a per-state workspace in state. Drop B3 (o m=128) and the o/unpooler m=256 cells of B4: the toggle profile shows Lt launches the identical nvjet kernel there. With those changes the per-cell gates make the run readable without a companion.
justification: A. Source A (bulk row-owner kernel, pooler m=1 only) is justified. Its paired 1.226x vs master's 1.135x on the largest decode_1 cell is a measured kernel-level win (17.0 vs 18.7 us), and gating it to m==1 matches where it won. Source B's qkv_gate m=128 evidence is real: under the Lt preference, profile 20 of 5ed9ace1 shows one nvjet_sm90_tst_48x64_64x15_4x2_h_bz_TNN at 16.2 us with no splitKreduce, against master's 96x64 splitK 12.7 + reduce 3.0 us. The mechanism is NOT 'the preference' as such. The algo-pick log (26a8be34) shows the Lt heuristic at a 32 MiB workspace returns, for qkv m=128, 8 candidates that are all splitK>=2. Its candidate 0 is bit-identical to torch's cuBLAS output (rel_vs_torch=0). So at matched inputs, cublasGemmEx and Lt pick the same algo. The 48x64 one-node kernel therefore comes from a different heuristic input in ATen's bgemm_internal_cublaslt: most likely a smaller Lt workspace cap that excludes the 2.36 MB split-K candidates, or ATen's alignment/descriptor attributes. An extension can reproduce that legally by querying at those caps in prepare(). The B2-B4 conjecture ('Lt drops the reduce node, so pooler NN m=128 goes 23.2 -> ~21') is weakly justified. The same toggle run already showed what Lt does at m=128 on TN. Pooler took a single-node 64x64 tile at 24.1 us (row 25.14), slower than master's NN splitK+reduce row of 23.2. Unpooler went 21.9 us, worse than master's NN 19.6. Dropping the reduce node by giving up split-K leaves a 4096x128 output at 128x64 tiles: 64 CTAs on 132 SMs, which is unlikely to beat split-K plus a 3 us reduce. o m=128 (128x64 TNT), o m=256 (128x128 TNT) and unpooler m=256 (128x128 TNT) ran the identical kernel under Lt and under cuBLAS, so those B3/B4 cells are null by construction. The expected directions in the hypothesis (pooler v16 faster, others unchanged/gate decides) are consistent with TASK weights. verify_16/verify_32 are 2 of 6 loads, and the realistic upside of B2-B4 is ~0-1 us on one cell, below the ~1.5% row noise, so it is readable only from the PATH CHOSEN lines and the profile. Weakest link: whether a rules-clean extension can actually reproduce the 48x64 single-node qkv algo. If the cause is an ATen descriptor attribute rather than the workspace cap, the heuristic ladder may never return it, and B collapses to master. A second weak link is the gate itself. In 26a8be34, a prepare-time graph-replay pick at a 0.97 threshold chose qkv m=256 cand 4 (26.27 vs 28.19 us), and that cell then LOST 0.962 in the judge. Prepare medians of 24 us vs judge rows of 16.8 us show how far that harness was from the judge's. This hypothesis uses the better _ouns_gate method (interleaved, empty-graph baseline subtracted), but at a looser 0.98 threshold.
confounders: pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256 (landed, nn_p256_ok): B4's pooler m=256 incumbent is this NN path (nvjet 128x64 NNT 29.5 us). B4 compares NN-under-Lt against it, so a B4 pooler gain is relative to the landed NN path, not to SGLang's TN. A self-check MISS on that cell must switch off the Lt flag, not nn_p256_ok.

restack-three-cell-wins-router-unpooler-cluster-m8-nn-m128 (landed, nn_ok for pooler/unpooler m=65..128): B2 replaces exactly the NN cuBLAS call this landed. master's _ab_selfcheck maps a pooler/unpooler m=128 MISS to nn_ok via _ab_component. If B2 routes there, a MISS caused by the Lt algo would switch off the proven NN path and fall back to TN cuBLAS, a confounded loss. _ab_component and _ab_flags must learn the new Lt and bulk flags.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (landed): defines the _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl incumbent for qkv m=128 (source B). It is the control, not a confounder, provided the extension builds the same TN problem (a77cdec6 did: rel_vs_torch=0 for cand 0).

bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32 / restack-three-cell-wins (pooler m=1 swapab16 incumbent): source A is checked before the swapab16 branch for pooler m==1 only. _ab_component returns '' for pooler m=1, so an A/B self-check MISS on the bulk kernel prints 'nothing to switch off' and the bulk path stays live. Add a bulk flag to _ab_component and _ab_flags.

Sibling queue item combo-naive-pooler-m1-rowowner-qkv-m128-cublaslt is this hypothesis minus B2-B4. If the B2-B4 gates all choose master (the likely outcome), the two submits are behaviourally identical. Run only one of them.
interference: No companion is warranted. Every added cell is behind its own prepare-time gate. Each gate prints a PATH CHOSEN line with both medians and is backed by a torch.profiler kernel-name assertion, so each changed scored row maps to a logged choice. Rows where master was chosen are byte-identical in dispatch. A gain reads as the sum of the cells that chose their candidate. A loss on a chosen cell reads as 'gate timing did not transfer to the judge', as with qkv m=256 in 26a8be34, and that is the finding. Source A was measured alone on this cell. A source-B-only control duplicates the sibling combo. A revert of the landed NN paths would only change B2/B4's incumbent, and the gate already prints that incumbent's median. A companion would cost a scored run and would not change how either outcome is read.
rules_flags: REQUIRED CHANGE (policy, not the judge): the per-call save/set/restore of torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library('cublaslt') around _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl is per-call mutable process-global state in kernel_fn and is forbidden by standing policy, even though the judge's static check passed it once (5ed9ace1). Replace source B and every B2-B4 cell with a prepare-time cuBLASLt plan held in state. Port _LT_CPP / _lt_build / _lt_forward from branch hyp/muse_bf16_proj/bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256 (impl a77cdec6; patch muse_bf16_proj/hypotheses/done/neutral/bf16-cublaslt-algo-pick-in-prepare-m128-m256.patch), extended in two ways. (i) NN descriptors (A = state[layer+'_t'], CUBLAS_OP_N) for the pooler/unpooler NN cells. (ii) cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic queried at a workspace-cap ladder {0, 1 MiB, 4 MiB, 32 MiB}, plus ATen's alignment preferences, with every candidate's tile/splitK/reduction printed. In prepare(), choose the algo row from that pooled candidate list through the cell's gate. kernel_fn branches on cfg plus state flags only and calls ext.run(x, W, out, state algo row, state workspace). No preference calls anywhere in kernel_fn, and no 'Lt warm-up under the preference' in prepare.

Keep a77cdec6's precision guards: exclude split-K candidates whose reduction scheme is not COMPUTE_TYPE (bf16 INPLACE/OUTPUT_TYPE reductions), and exclude any candidate whose fp64 error exceeds 1.10x the incumbent's.

Per-state Lt workspace (one uint8 buffer per routed cell per state). The C++ descriptor cache is keyed by shape only and holds no device pointers, which is acceptable. The second A/B state must allocate its own workspace and inherit only the algo rows and flags.
Source A's state['bulk_route_hit'] write in _bulk_forward must be dropped (already in the spec); confirm by grep before submit.
_ab_component and _ab_flags must cover the new components (bulk pooler m=1, each Lt cell), so a self-check MISS switches off the right flag and never nn_ok / nn_p256_ok.

No other rules concerns. Weights are unchanged (bulk repack is a verified lossless permutation; Lt uses stored bf16 weights or the existing lossless transpose). Precision is bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out. All selection happens in untimed prepare() on synthetic data. There are no syncs or value-sized allocations in kernel_fn.
open_questions: Does any heuristic query at a workspace cap below the 2.36 MB split-K requirement return the nvjet 48x64_64x15 no-splitK algo for qkv_gate m=128? Print the candidate table per cap. If none does, the cause is an ATen descriptor attribute: replicate bgemm_internal_cublaslt's descriptor (alignment prefs, transposes, ld) before concluding source B is unreachable.
Should the gate threshold be 0.97 with the _ouns_gate harness, or stay at 0.98? 26a8be34's 0.97 pick on qkv m=256 lost 3.8% in the judge, and the B cells differ by only 1-3 us.
Should B2 also require the profile to show no splitKreduce node? The conjecture is specifically about node count, so a B2 candidate that wins the gate while keeping split-K tells a different story.

With B3 and the null B4 cells dropped (o m=128/256, unpooler m=256: identical kernels under Lt in 5ed9ace1), do the remaining probes (pooler/unpooler m=128 NN, pooler m=256 NN) justify a separate scored submit over the sibling combo, or should B2/B4 be folded into the sibling and this slug retired?
